searchText: Immutable X is currently a validium, with a future upgrade planned to volition Validium = Proofs on-chain, data availability off-chain Volition = Giving users the choice between validium and rollup The optimism sequencer is also centralised. And they’ve promised any profit made during this period of decentralising will go to public goods It actually works pretty well and it’s super fast. The main issue I see with optimism currently is the tx fees. $3 to send usdc is not cheap and there is nothing they can do about it, as they depend on L1 Wait really? Why is it so high? Because layer 1 has high fees still Do they need higher overall throughput in order to be able to amortize the costs better? Optimism is the one running Synthetix and Uniswap right? “That's not something we can control. To provide guaranteed availability we have to publish all transaction data on L1. The cheapest way to do this is CALLDATA, but that's still 16 gas per non-zero byte (and 4 per byte that stores zero). That's where most of our transaction cost comes from.” They need lower gas prices on l1 Yes but most stuff on them is NFT and they're still even unable to transfer NFT from them to L1, so what data is stored there? how is zksync able to have fees for transfers as low as 0.0000822 eth then? which is ~26 cents I understand how the L1 gas costs are the limiting factor here but then does optimism use a less efficient L1 representation for transfers? Optimism throughput is being artificially restricted today. Optimism also runs on geth which has limited scalability As for data representation, ZK rollups are capable of fundamnetally better ways of compressing data than naive ORU :-x

Volition = Giving users the choice between validium and rollup
